facts.fact: Over 88 million U.S. households stream TV content, according to Nielsen.
facts.quote: Over 88 million U.S. households now stream TV content, according to Nielsen.

facts.fact: eMarketer projects that by 2026, 60% of U.S. households will have cut the cord or never subscribed to pay TV.
facts.quote: eMarketer projects that by 2026: 60% of U.S. households will have cut the cord or never subscribed to pay TV

facts.fact: eMarketer projects that CTV/streaming will capture 45% of all TV viewing time by 2026.
facts.quote: CTV/streaming will capture 45% of all TV viewing time

facts.fact: eMarketer projects 73 million households will be "cord-never" (never had traditional pay TV) by 2026.
facts.quote: 73 million households will be "cord-never" (never had traditional pay TV)

facts.fact: 79% of adults aged 18-34 use streaming services as their primary TV source.
facts.quote: 79% of adults 18-34 use streaming services as their primary TV source.

facts.fact: In the page's illustrative state senate example, a broadcast DMA buy covers 1.2 million households, with 80% waste, versus CTV targeting only the 200,000 district households.
facts.quote: Buy the entire DMA (1.2 million households), 80% waste

facts.fact: The vendor claims that at similar CPMs, CTV delivers 5x more relevant impressions than broadcast TV in its state senate example.
facts.quote: At similar CPMs, CTV delivers 5x more relevant impressions.

facts.fact: CTV advertising has no minimums on self-serve platforms, and campaigns can start with $50.
facts.quote: CTV advertising has no minimums on self-serve platforms. Campaigns can start with $50 and scale based on performance and funds raised.

facts.fact: Traditional minimum broadcast TV buys are $5,000-50,000.
facts.quote: Minimum broadcast TV buys: $5,000-50,000

facts.fact: Premium direct-sold CTV inventory typically requires a significant minimum spend of $50,000 or more and advance booking.
facts.quote: Typically requires significant minimum spend ($50,000+) and advance booking.

facts.fact: Historically, political campaigns needed six-figure budgets for broadcast TV advertising.
facts.quote: Where campaigns once needed six-figure budgets for broadcast TV, CTV makes TV advertising accessible

facts.fact: The page states that a standard political spot on CTV is 30 seconds long.
facts.quote: 30 seconds: Standard political spot

facts.fact: The page expects 50-70% match rates when matching clean voter files to streaming household audiences.
facts.quote: Expect 50-70% match rates for clean voter files.

facts.fact: Premium political CTV inventory (Hulu, Peacock, direct) is priced at $30-50 CPM in 2026.
facts.quote: **Premium inventory (Hulu, Peacock, direct):** $30-50 CPM

facts.fact: Mid-tier political CTV inventory (Roku, Samsung TV+) is priced at $20-35 CPM in 2026.
facts.quote: **Mid-tier inventory (Roku, Samsung TV+):** $20-35 CPM

facts.fact: FAST channel political CTV inventory (Tubi, Pluto) is priced at $12-25 CPM in 2026.
facts.quote: **FAST channels (Tubi, Pluto):** $12-25 CPM

facts.fact: Programmatic mix political CTV inventory is priced at $20-35 CPM in 2026.
facts.quote: **Programmatic mix:** $20-35 CPM

facts.fact: Political CTV CPMs are expected to be 20-40% higher in October than in February.
facts.quote: Expect 20-40% higher CPMs in October compared to February.

facts.fact: Recommended total CTV budget for congressional/Senate races is $100,000-1,000,000+.
facts.quote: Total CTV budget: $100,000-1,000,000+

facts.fact: Recommended total CTV budget for state legislative races is $15,000-100,000.
facts.quote: Total CTV budget: $15,000-100,000

facts.fact: Recommended total CTV budget for local races (city, county, school board) is $3,000-25,000.
facts.quote: Total CTV budget: $3,000-25,000

facts.fact: Recommended frequency goal for congressional/Senate CTV campaigns is 10-15+ impressions per household.
facts.quote: Frequency goal: 10-15+ impressions per household

facts.fact: Recommended frequency goal for state legislative CTV campaigns is 8-12 impressions per household.
facts.quote: Frequency goal: 8-12 impressions per household

facts.fact: Recommended frequency goal for local race CTV campaigns is 6-10 impressions per household.
facts.quote: Frequency goal: 6-10 impressions per household

facts.fact: The page recommends allocating 10-20% of budget to creative testing.
facts.quote: Allocate 10-20% of budget to creative testing, especially early in campaigns

facts.fact: Minimum recommended resolution for political CTV ads is 1080p (1920x1080).
facts.quote: **Resolution:** 1080p minimum (1920x1080). 4K helpful but not essential.

facts.fact: Standard aspect ratio for political CTV ads is 16:9.
facts.quote: **Aspect ratio:** 16:9 standard for TV screens.

facts.fact: Most CTV platforms accept MP4 files with H.264 encoding.
facts.quote: **File formats:** Most platforms accept MP4 with H.264 encoding.

facts.fact: Streaming platforms typically require creative review periods of 24-72 hours.
facts.quote: **Advance submission:** Plan for creative review periods of 24-72 hours.

facts.fact: Typical CTV ad completion rate is 90% or higher, according to the page.
facts.quote: **Completion rate:** Percentage of ads watched to completion (typically 90%+ on CTV)

facts.fact: The page's example state senate race CTV plan with a $25,000 budget at $25 CPM yields 1,000,000 impressions and 6.7 frequency across 150,000 households.
facts.quote: **Frequency:** 6.7 impressions per household (1,000,000 / 150,000)

facts.fact: In the page's example, a $8,000 broadcast spot reaches 500,000 households, of which 30% are in-district.
facts.quote: Compare to broadcast TV in the same market at $8,000 per spot reaching 500,000 households (only 30% in district):

facts.fact: CTV political advertising typically costs $20-35 CPM for programmatic inventory.
facts.quote: CTV political advertising typically costs $20-35 CPM for programmatic inventory, with premium inventory at $30-50 CPM.

facts.fact: Premium CTV inventory for political advertising typically costs $30-50 CPM.
facts.quote: with premium inventory at $30-50 CPM.

facts.fact: At $25 CPM, a $5,000 budget delivers 200,000 impressions.
facts.quote: At $25 CPM, a $5,000 budget delivers 200,000 impressions.

facts.fact: Adwave's self-serve platform allows campaigns to start from $30 a day.
facts.quote: Self-serve platforms like Adwave allow campaigns to start from $30 a day and scale based on performance and fundraising.

facts.fact: A city council campaign can run effective CTV advertising for $3,000-5,000 by targeting only its district.
facts.quote: A city council campaign can run effective CTV advertising for $3,000-5,000 by targeting only their district.

facts.fact: Match rates for voter file matching to streaming households typically range 50-70% for clean voter files.
facts.quote: Match rates typically range 50-70% for clean voter files.

facts.fact: Platforms may require advertiser verification before approving political content, which can take several days.
facts.quote: Platforms may also require advertiser verification before approving political content. Complete verification early as it can take several days.

facts.fact: Political CTV ads require 'Paid for by' disclosures identifying the sponsoring committee.
facts.quote: Political CTV ads require "Paid for by" disclosures identifying the sponsoring committee, similar to broadcast TV requirements.

facts.fact: The recommended launch timeline begins complete platform verification 8-12 weeks before the election.
facts.quote: **8-12 weeks before election:** Complete platform verification

facts.fact: CTV targeting can use congressional district, state legislative district, or municipal boundaries, whereas broadcast buys cover entire DMAs.
facts.quote: CTV enables congressional district, state legislative district, or even municipal boundary targeting.
